explanations: terra: The hypocrites are likened to one who kindles a fire that lights the surroundings before God removes its light; an outwardly successful flame becomes darkness, like outward prayer emptied of care.

luna: The fire’s fuel is people and stones rather than household fuel, reversing the source’s ordinary hearth and making the movement from useful fire to punishment explicit. | terra: The warned fire has people and stones as its fuel; the section's ordinary fuel for a useful hearth is reversed so the unjust become the fuel.
terra: The covenant joins good treatment of parents, kin, orphans, and the poor with upright speech, prayer, and zakāh; it directly reverses worship severed from vulnerable neighbors.
luna: They eat only fire into their bellies; this reverses the source’s cooked meal into punishment.

luna: The next verse calls this a trade of guidance for error and punishment; 2:174 supplies the image of fire eaten as food. | terra: "فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ" confronts people who traded guidance with what it means to bear fire, closely matching the dictionary sense of enduring an affair's heat and severity.
terra: Righteousness includes giving loved wealth to kin, orphans, the poor, travelers, and petitioners, then establishing prayer and zakāh; shared provision and ṣalāt form one integrity.
terra: When believers ask what to spend, the answer names parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and the traveler; available good is routed toward the same vulnerable people excluded in surah 107.
terra: Charity performed "رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ" is voided by its motive; the same showing-off root exposes why an outward act cannot compensate for a heart closed to others.
terra: Neither wealth nor children will avail the disbelievers, who are themselves "وَقُودُ النَّارِ"; hoarded means fail and their owners become fuel.
terra: People do not attain full righteousness until they spend from what they love; the valued store must be opened, the opposite of retaining even minor useful goods.
terra: Those who withhold God's bounty are warned that what they withheld will be hung around their necks on Resurrection; the retained possession itself becomes punishment.

luna: The verse turns wrongful consumption of orphan wealth into fire in the belly and a coming searing; the source’s ordinary food and hearth are reversed into punishment. | terra: Those who consume orphans' property eat fire into their bellies and "سَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا"; abuse of the vulnerable turns food itself into the fire carried by the section's prayer-root.
terra: Whoever commits aggression and injustice will be made to enter fire, "فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نَارًا"; the root's burning sense is tied to violating others' rights.
terra: Worship of God is joined to good treatment of parents, kin, orphans, the miskīn, neighbors, travelers, and dependents; devotion is tested across the whole household and social circle.
terra: The proud are those who are miserly, command miserliness, and conceal God's bounty; it expands the active withholding condemned in the section.
terra: Those who spend only to be seen by people and disbelieve in God and the Last Day combine ostentation, material action, and denial exactly as surah 107 diagnoses them.

luna: The fire repeatedly cooks the skin until it is replaced so the person can taste punishment; the source’s cooking and roasting branch turns from meat to the one facing fire. | terra: God will "نُصْلِيهِمْ نَارًا" and replace their skins whenever they are cooked through; the ayah unites the root's burning sense with the section's roasting image.
terra: The one who breaks with the Messenger and follows another way is consigned to Hell with "نُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ", confirming the root's fire sense.
terra: The hypocrites rise lazily to prayer "يُرَاءُونَ النَّاسَ" and remember God little; it directly explains the showy, inattentive prayer named in 107:5-6.
terra: Expiation includes feeding ten poor people from the average food one feeds one's own family; the domestic table becomes the measure for sharing with the miskīn.
terra: True believers establish prayer and spend from what God provided; giving is presented as a coordinate sign of the same faith.
terra: The opponents' prayer at the House is reduced to whistling and clapping, then they are told to taste punishment for disbelief; empty ritual does not shield from judgment.

luna: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend face a warning of painful punishment; the source likewise moves from withheld household provision to fire. | terra: Hoarders of gold and silver who do not spend in God's path are warned of painful punishment; the withheld store becomes the material heated in the next ayah.

luna: Here hoarded wealth is heated in the Fire and used to brand its holders; 9:34 supplies the hoarding that this punishment answers. | terra: The hoarded metal is heated in Hell and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs; what was withheld becomes both furnace-work and torment.
terra: Their contributions are rejected because they disbelieve, come to prayer lazily, and spend unwillingly; failed worship and failed giving are diagnosed together.
terra: Those who evade the campaign rejoice at staying behind and dislike striving in heat, but are told Hell is fiercer in heat; avoiding present heat does not spare them the heat to be endured.

terra: Charity is taken from wealth and the Prophet is told to pray for the givers, for "إِنَّ صَلَاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَّهُمْ"; the two roots the section joins, prayer ص ل و and repose س ك ن, here meet through giving rather than withholding.
terra: The Flood's onset is marked when the tannūr erupts; an ordinary oven or hearth becomes the sign that domestic security has given way to judgment.
terra: Abraham quickly brings his guests a roasted calf; the section's cooked-meat hearth appears here as generous hospitality rather than private consumption.
terra: Shuʿayb's people ask whether his prayer commands them to abandon what they please to do with their wealth; even their taunt recognizes that ṣalāt reaches economic conduct.
terra: The wretched in the Fire have audible exhaling and inhaling, giving the punitive flame and its occupants the harsh sound the section hears behind its fire-bearing name.
terra: Material is heated in fire to make ornaments or useful goods, and its dross rises away; this is the Qur'an's clearest parallel to fire making resistant material fit for a purpose.
terra: "جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا" describes those who exchanged God's favor for disbelief entering Hell, another exact burning use of the named root.
terra: Believing servants are commanded to establish prayer and spend secretly and openly before the irreversible Day, answering both ostentation and withholding.

terra: Abraham says "أَسْكَنْتُ" of settling his family by the Sacred House, then asks that they establish prayer and be provided fruits; dwelling, prayer, and provision meet in one household petition.
terra: Livestock are said to provide warmth, benefits, and food; although fire is absent, the ayah gathers the same household functions of warming and eating that the section locates at the hearth.
terra: God makes human houses "سَكَنًا", places of rest; this primary Qur'anic sense of the poor-person root sets the shared shelter against a home whose implements are withheld.
terra: The person who wants only the immediate world is assigned Hell "يَصْلَاهَا مَذْمُومًا مَّدْحُورًا"; ص ل و marks the final exposure after self-directed appetite.
terra: The relative, the miskīn, and the traveler must be given their due; the poor person's claim is treated as a right, not discretionary leftovers.
terra: The hand must be neither chained to the neck nor extended without limit; this sets a concrete boundary against the closed fist while preserving responsible household provision.
terra: Hell's drink is like molten metal "يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ"; the section's dictionary example of roasting meat is grimly transferred to human faces.

luna: The verse heats iron with bellows and pours molten copper to form a barrier; it does not straighten a stick, but it is a specific parallel to the source’s fire softening material so it can be shaped. | terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn heats iron blocks until they are like fire and then pours molten copper over them; controlled heat transforms hard material into a protective structure.
terra: Jesus says God enjoined prayer and zakāh upon him throughout life, keeping worship and material duty together.
terra: Ishmael commands his household to prayer and zakāh; the home itself becomes a place where worship and giving are taught together.
terra: Later generations neglect prayer and follow desires, then meet ruin; it is a direct Qur'anic counterpart to being heedless of one's prayer.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in صِلِيًّا for burning; the verse identifies who is most deserving of that fire. | terra: God knows best who most deserves "صِلِيًّا" in Hell; the verbal noun preserves the root's sense of exposure to fire.
terra: Every person is said to come to Hell, establishing the shared boundary before the next ayah distinguishes those rescued from those left there.
terra: God rescues the mindful and leaves the wrongdoers kneeling in Hell; the ayah marks the final separation within the fire scene introduced by 19:70-71.

luna: Moses asks his family to wait while he seeks a firebrand; warmth is not stated here, but the household fire carried back is a plausible parallel to the source’s hearth image. | terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring his family a brand or find guidance at it; it is the parallel family-fire scene completed with the warming verb in 27:7 and 28:29.
terra: The criminal in Hell neither dies nor lives; unending suspension makes concrete the dictionary sense of having to bear an affair's heat and severity.
terra: Abraham's enemies command one another to burn him, converting communal zeal into a human furnace; the next ayah marks fire's divinely imposed boundary.

luna: God commands Abraham’s fire to be coolness and safety; this is a specific reversal of the source’s ordinary heat and its final burning punishment. | terra: God tells the fire to be coolness and safety for Abraham; fire that was meant as torment becomes shelter, sharply separating destructive flame from protective warmth.
terra: The condemned have a groaning sound in Hell and cannot hear there; the fire scene is explicitly acoustic rather than merely visual.
terra: Boiling liquid melts what is inside the condemned and their skins; punitive heat takes on the section's cooking and softening actions.
terra: Whenever they try to leave the anguish they are returned and told to taste the burning punishment; this is forced endurance of heat and severity.
luna: Pilgrims are told to eat sacrificial meat and feed the destitute poor; this joins the source’s meat and poor-food details in a concrete sharing scene.
terra: The humbly fearful establish prayer and spend from God's provision; reverent worship opens the hand rather than closing it.
luna: After the sacrificial animals fall, people are told to eat and feed the contented and the needy; it turns the source’s withheld meat and hearth into a shared meal.
terra: Successful believers are humble in their prayer, opposing the prayer performed for display.
terra: The same portrait makes them active in zakāh, so inwardly humble prayer issues in material care.
terra: They guard their prayers, completing the reversal of negligence toward prayer.
terra: The repeated Flood account again begins rescue when the tannūr erupts, preserving the striking reversal of the household oven into a catastrophic boundary.
terra: People of means are forbidden to swear off giving to relatives, the poor, and emigrants and are told to pardon; a self-imposed refusal to share is explicitly revoked.
terra: The lamp in a niche, glass, and oil almost glowing before fire supply a luminous household fire-image; 24:37 then joins remembrance to prayer and zakāh.
terra: The lamp image is carried into houses where God's name is remembered morning and evening; the next ayah identifies occupants whose prayer and giving survive worldly distraction.
terra: Trade does not distract these people from remembrance, prayer, or zakāh, and they fear the Day; attentive prayer, giving, and judgment-consciousness answer all three failures of surah 107.

terra: The detailed household rule permits eating from relatives' and friends' houses and says there is no blame in eating together or separately; the home table is structured for access rather than jealous closure.
terra: When Hell sees them from afar they hear its fury and roaring; this gives literal fire-sound to the section's claim that the name can be heard with fire in it.
terra: Cast bound into a narrow place of the Fire, the condemned call there for destruction; the fire elicits the calamity-cry heard in وَيْل.
terra: They are told not to call for one destruction but for many, intensifying the ruin-cry attached to entering the fire.
terra: God's servants are neither extravagant nor stingy when they spend, placing generosity within a measured middle rather than the section's outright refusal.

luna: Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring a brand so his family may تَصْطَلُونَ, matching the source dictionary form اصطليت بالنار for warming at a hearth. | terra: Moses sees a fire and promises his family a burning brand "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ" so they may warm themselves; the verb directly realizes the section's dictionary scene اصطليت بالنار of a shared household fire.

luna: Moses promises a firebrand لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ, the same warming scene and root sense as the source’s اصطليت بالنار. | terra: Moses asks his family to wait while he seeks news or a firebrand "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ"; this repeats the section's exact secondary sense of ص ل و, warming oneself at a fire rather than burning in punishment.

terra: Abraham's people answer his message by proposing that he be killed or burned, but God saves him from the fire; the repeated Abraham scene separates humanly intended furnace from divinely granted safety.
terra: Prayer is said to restrain indecency and recognized wrong; a prayer compatible with repelling the vulnerable and withholding aid fails this stated function.
terra: The relative, miskīn, and traveler are again to receive their due, and such giving is named the path to success.

luna: The source’s dictionary image softens a crooked stick with fire before straightening it; here God makes iron soft for David, a specific material-softening parallel, though this verse does not mention fire. | terra: God softens iron for David; although fire is not named, the specific softening of rigid material may echo the section's fire-softened stick.
terra: David is told to fashion armor and measure its links; with 34:10, the softened material is deliberately made fit, though the section's straightening-by-fire link remains indirect.
terra: Solomon's workers make large serving basins and fixed cauldrons and are told to work gratefully; abundant household vessels are framed as gifts demanding gratitude, not objects to withhold.
terra: Whatever people spend, God replaces, and He is the best provider; fear of depletion is answered by the Provider behind the household store.
terra: Those who recite God's book establish prayer and spend secretly and openly, hoping in a trade that will not perish; their prayer circulates provision instead of hoarding it.
terra: The punishment of Hell is neither ended by death nor lightened, another direct portrayal of fire as severity that must continually be endured.

luna: When urged to give from their provision, the deniers refuse to feed those God could feed; that answer closely echoes the source’s withheld food before its turn to fire. | terra: When told to spend from God's provision, the disbelievers refuse to feed those God could have fed; disbelief becomes an argument for withholding food.
terra: "اصْلَوْهَا الْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ" is a direct command to enter the fire because of disbelief, joining the root's fire sense to denial.
terra: God makes fire for people from the green tree, and they kindle from it; the usable hearth is itself provided rather than privately self-created.
luna: The question contrasts good hospitality with the Zaqqum tree; it brings the source’s hearth and meal image into a stark judgment reversal.
luna: The sinners eat from the tree and fill their bellies; 37:62 introduces the rival meal and 37:67-68 complete the Hell setting.
luna: Their meal is mixed with boiling water; 37:66 gives the eating, transforming the source’s cooked food into torment.
luna: Their return is to Hell after the meal; 37:66-67 supply the food and boiling drink, completing the source’s food-to-fire reversal.
terra: Those who follow false gods can mislead only one destined to be "صَالِ الْجَحِيمِ"; the participle shares the section's root in its burning sense.
terra: The transgressors have Hell "يَصْلَوْنَهَا", another direct use of ص ل و for entering and bearing the fire.
terra: After Hell is named in 38:56, the condemned are told to taste boiling and foul fluids; the burning place supplies an anti-meal instead of sustaining provision.
terra: The condemned are dragged through boiling water and then stoked in the fire, turning the actions of a heated vessel and furnace upon their bodies.
terra: "وَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ" sounds the same disaster cry as 107:4, and the next ayah defines its targets through refusal of zakāh and denial of the afterlife.
terra: Those under the وَيْل neither give zakāh nor believe in the Hereafter, tightly joining withheld material due with the denial that opens surah 107.
terra: Those who answer their Lord establish prayer, consult together, and spend from provision; worship is embedded in shared communal action.
terra: The criminals remain in Hell's punishment, stating the persistence of the heat rather than a momentary contact with it.
terra: The punishment is not eased and they despair within it, completing the image of being made to bear unrelieved severity.

luna: The Zaqqum tree introduces a judgment meal; 44:44 calls it sinners’ food, reversing the source’s ordinary hearth and cooked meat. | terra: The tree of Zaqqūm introduces the food that will boil inside the sinner before he is dragged into the blaze, turning nourishment into the opening of a punitive meal.

luna: The tree is explicitly طَعَامُ الْأَثِيمِ, food for the sinner; 44:43 introduces it and 44:45-46 make its heat bodily. | terra: Zaqqūm is identified as the food of the sinner; food, the object denied to the poor in the section, becomes punishment in the coming fire scene.

luna: This food boils in the belly like molten metal; 44:44 names it as a meal, turning the source’s cooking image into punishment. | terra: The food is like molten substance boiling in bellies, transferring the actions of a pot and furnace into the condemned body.

luna: The meal boils like حمِيم; 44:45 gives the belly where it boils, extending the source’s fire and food image. | terra: Its boiling is compared to fiercely heated water, completing the punitive cooking image before the prisoner is seized.

luna: The sinner is dragged to the middle of Hell; 44:43-46 have already made the meal and its boiling explicit, joining food to the fire destination. | terra: "خُذُوهُ" orders the sinner seized and dragged into the middle of Hell, closely repeating the staged command of 69:30-31.

luna: Boiling water is poured over his head after he is dragged to Hell; 44:47 supplies the destination and this verse completes the heat scene. | terra: Boiling torment is poured over his head, joining the vessel's heated contents to bodily punishment.

luna: The command ذُقْ tells him to taste the punishment; 44:48 supplies the boiling water, echoing the source’s tasting and enduring fire senses. | terra: The prisoner is commanded to taste, making him personally undergo the heat and severity that the section's dictionary sense describes.

luna: The punishment is identified as what they doubted; 44:49 commands them to taste it, joining denial to the source’s fire consequence. | terra: He is told that this is what he used to doubt, so the cooked food and blaze answer denial just as fire answers denial elsewhere in the section.
terra: Some who are called to spend instead withhold, and the ayah says their withholding turns against themselves; the closed hand creates its owner's loss.

luna: The command أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ places the condemned figure in Hell; 50:25 identifies him as a preventer of good, completing the source’s withholding-to-fire link. | terra: The paired command to throw every stubborn ingrate into Hell stages the final exposure to fire immediately before the withholding epithet in 50:25.

luna: The condemned person is called مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ, a preventer of good; 50:24 supplies the command to cast him into Hell, matching the withheld shared hearth and its consequence. | terra: "مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ" names the condemned as a persistent preventer of good, the same social action as refusing the small aid of 107:7.
terra: The Godfearing assign in their wealth a due for the asker and the deprived, anticipating the explicit recognized share of the prayerful in 70:24-25.
terra: Abraham slips away to his household and brings a fat calf, making the household store serve an unexpected guest.
terra: He places the food before the guests and invites them to eat; the act supplies the open table missing from the section's withheld hearth.
terra: "فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ" announces woe to the deniers just before they are pushed into Hell in 52:13, completing another woe-denial-fire unit.
terra: Deniers are violently pushed "إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا"; the exact pushing verb used of the orphan in 107:2 is returned upon them at the fire.
terra: They are told, "هَٰذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ"; the fire is explicitly identified as the reality their denial rejected.
luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in اصْلَوْهَا; the command says to burn there whether patient or impatient, directly meeting its dictionary sense of bearing heat.
luna: This addresses astray deniers immediately before 56:52-56 describe their judgment meal, joining denial to the source’s meal-to-fire movement.
luna: The deniers’ meal is from the Zaqqum tree, reversing the source’s hearth food into punishment; 56:54-56 make the boiling and judgment setting explicit.
luna: They fill their bellies from this food; 56:52 names the meal, turning the source’s cooking and sharing image inward.
luna: They drink boiling water over the meal; 56:52-53 supply the food and full bellies, continuing the inverted feast.
luna: They drink like thirsty camels; 56:54 supplies the boiling drink, extending the punishment meal linked against the source’s hearth.
luna: This meal is named their hospitality on the Day of Judgment; 56:52-55 show the food and drink, contrasting with the home hearth’s hospitality.

luna: The verse asks about the fire people kindle, directly meeting the source’s domestic fire and its ordinary uses. | terra: The hearers are asked to consider the fire they kindle, bringing the ordinary human hearth itself into view.

luna: It asks who created the fire’s tree; 56:71 names the kindled fire and 56:73 gives its provision for travelers. | terra: God asks whether people created the fire's tree or He did, relocating ownership of even the hearth's fuel from the possessive householder to the Provider.

luna: The fire is made مَتَاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ, provision for travelers; 56:71-72 identify it as kindled and created, an explicit useful-fire counterpart to the punishment fire. | terra: God made kindled fire both a reminder and a benefit for travelers; its warmth and utility are provision to be received, while its reminder points beyond the domestic flame.

luna: The condemned group is called deniers gone astray; 56:93-94 give their fiery reception, joining denial to the source’s end. | terra: The dying person is identified as one of the denying and astray, establishing the stance whose hostile reception follows in 56:93-94.

luna: Their welcome is boiling water, a dreadful inversion of food and hospitality at the source’s hearth; 56:94 names Hellfire next. | terra: His first reception is scalding water, the heated drink immediately paired with burning in Hell in 56:94.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in تَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ, explicitly naming burning in Hell after the boiling-water welcome of 56:93. | terra: "وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ" names the hostile reception of a denier as burning in Hell, using the same root as the section's prayer-name.
terra: Those who are miserly and command others to miserliness repeat the section's failure both to give and to urge care.
terra: The hosts prefer others over themselves despite their own need and are saved from inner stinginess; this is the communal home opposite to refusing even small household aid.
terra: Believers are told to listen, obey, and spend, and those guarded from their own stinginess prosper; release from inner withholding is made the condition of success.

terra: Divorced women must be lodged where the household dwells, supported according to means, and not harmed; the root س ك ن appears within an explicit duty of shelter and material care, reversing the closed home of the section.

luna: The command to protect one’s family from a fire fueled by people and stones turns the household hearth into its opposite. | terra: Believers must protect themselves and their households from a fire whose fuel is people and stones; the domestic responsibility of a household is framed against the unshareable final fire.
terra: When people are thrown into Hell they hear it inhaling or roaring as it boils, again making punitive fire an audible presence.
terra: "مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ" repeats 50:25's exact characterization of the habitual preventer of good, clarifying the disposition behind refusing al-māʿūn.
terra: The garden owners resolve that no miskīn shall enter the orchard that day; the poor person is deliberately excluded from available food.
terra: They set out early with firm power to withhold, turning the refusal of a poor person's share into a deliberate collective plan.
terra: When the crop is ruined, the withholders recognize that they themselves have become deprived; exclusion of the poor returns as their own deprivation.

luna: The source begins its Hāqqah account with the left-hand book recipient wishing he had never received his record; this regret starts the same condemned person’s approach to the fire quoted in 69:31. | terra: Receiving the record in the left hand prompts the wish that it had never been given; this begins the precise judgment sequence that reaches seizure and burning.

luna: This commands seizure and binding before 69:31’s burning; the row supplies the approach to the image’s final fire. | terra: "خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ" commands seizure and shackling, the first action in the staged movement completed by the fire command in 69:31.

luna: The source section names ص ل و as the root that also carries fire; here صَلُّوهُ orders him into Hell, making the fire-sense audible in the name musallīn. | terra: The command "ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ" uses the same ص ل و letters as الْمُصَلِّينَ in the section, now unambiguously for making the prisoner enter and endure Hell.

luna: The chain follows the command to burn him; 69:31 contributes the Hellfire, and this verse continues the punishment beyond entry. | terra: After the command to burn the prisoner, he is inserted into a long chain; this continues the staged handling begun by seizure and shackling in 69:30 rather than introducing a separate cause.

luna: The fire sequence names disbelief in God as a reason; 69:34 adds failure to urge food for the poor, placing this cause beside the shared-hearth image. | terra: The first stated cause is failure to believe in God the Great; paired with 69:34, it reproduces surah 107's inseparable denial and social neglect.

luna: This repeats the section’s wording about not urging food for the miskīn; the refusal is named beside the punishment, while the source links miskīn’s root س ك ن to a fire people settle beside. | terra: The condemned person "وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ"; its wording exactly repeats 107:3 and supplies the stated cause immediately after his consignment to the fire in 69:31.

luna: There is no close friend for him there; after the source’s hearth that could be shared, this gives the social emptiness of the fire-bound outcome. | terra: After refusing to encourage poor-feeding, the prisoner has no close friend that Day; denied social care returns as complete isolation.

luna: After the refusal to urge food for the poor in 69:34, this condemned person has no food except ghislin; 69:37 says who eats it, turning the source’s withheld meal into punishment. | terra: He has no food except foul discharge; the one who would not support the miskīn's food now faces an unshareable anti-meal.

luna: Only sinners eat the food named in 69:36; following the failure to feed the miskīn in 69:34, it sharpens the source’s passage from withheld food to fire. | terra: Only sinners eat that food, completing the reversal of wholesome food denied to the poor.

luna: This warning names لَظَىٰ, the flame that 70:16 says strips skin, making the source’s change from hearth to harm bodily. | terra: The warning "إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ" reveals the blaze that calls and receives the person who turns away and hoards in 70:17-18, completing the surah's withholding-to-fire sequence.

luna: The flame strips away the skin; 70:15 names the fire, echoing the source’s fire-roasted meat and endured heat. | terra: The blaze strips the body's outer parts; this gives the hoarder's fire a bodily action analogous to the section's roasting and heat-working imagery.
terra: The blaze calls the person who turned his back and turned away, making fire an active claimant of the same stance later excepted by true prayer.
terra: The one summoned by the blaze gathered wealth and stored it away; hoarded provision leads directly to fire before 70:21-25 oppose him with prayerful sharing.

luna: When good reaches a person, he is withholding; 70:22 immediately sets the prayerful apart, matching the source’s withholding beside its prayer word. | terra: The human being becomes "مَنُوعًا" when good reaches him; this is the same withholding root as وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ, immediately before the exception made for the prayerful.

luna: The source names al-muṣallīn; here the same word introduces those who pray as a commendable group, unlike the heedless prayer people of the source. | terra: "إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ" makes true prayer the explicit exception to withholding, reversing the section's الْمُصَلِّينَ who refuse ordinary aid.

luna: These prayerful people are constant in their prayer; 70:22 introduces the group whose care for others contrasts with the source’s prayer name over a fire image. | terra: These prayerful people are constant in their prayer, a precise reversal of those who are heedless of their prayer in 107:5.

luna: Their wealth has an acknowledged right; 70:25 assigns it to petitioners and deprived people, a direct counter-image to withholding the pot and ladle. | terra: True worshippers have a recognized right in their wealth; this makes material sharing an internal mark of prayer rather than an optional addition to it.

luna: The next verse names the recipients as سَائِلٍ وَالْمَحْرُومِ, making the share in 70:24 concrete against the source’s unfed poor. | terra: That recognized share belongs to the asker and the deprived, specifying the recipients whose exclusion exposes the section's false worshippers.
luna: The prayerful group believes in the Day of Recompense; 70:22-25 describe their prayer and share for the deprived, contrasting with the source’s heedless worship and the surah’s denier.
luna: They fear their Lord’s punishment; 70:22-25 give their prayer and wealth-sharing, the opposite of heedlessness before the source’s fire.
luna: They do not treat their Lord’s punishment as safe; 70:27 states their fear, contrasting with those who let the source’s warning go unheeded.
terra: These believers carefully guard their prayers, the direct opposite of being heedless of prayer in 107:5.
terra: The unjust become firewood for Hell; the domestic fuel named in the section is transformed into the fate of those who deviate.

luna: The source names ص ل و as fire; سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ uses that root for making a person burn in Saqar. | terra: "سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ" uses the named root in its punitive fire sense and introduces the very fire in which 74:43-46 connect prayer, poor-feeding, and denial.
luna: Saqar leaves nothing and spares nothing; 74:26 names the fire and 74:29 its scorching effect, extending the punishment scene around the source’s final fire.

luna: Saqar is described as لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ, scorching human skin; 74:26 names the fire, giving bodily force to the source’s heat and roasting image. | terra: Saqar scorches human skin, specifying the bodily action of the fire introduced with the ص ل و verb in 74:26.

terra: The people of the right ask the prisoners what brought them into Saqar; this question explicitly makes the fire the destination explained by their failures in prayer, feeding, and belief in 74:43-46.

luna: In Hell they say لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ; the source names musallīn and its fire-bearing root, while this confession gives the prayer failure behind the punishment. | terra: The people of Saqar answer "لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ"; prayer is named inside the fire interrogation whose next answer is failure to feed the poor.

luna: They confess they did not feed the miskīn, echoing the source’s food and poor image; its root س ك ن also carries the section’s hearth association. | terra: The next confession is "وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ"; it directly places refusal to feed the poor beside prayer and Saqar, the conjunction developed by the section.

luna: They confess that they denied the Day of Recompense; 74:43-44 place failure to pray and feed the poor in the same account of those facing punishment. | terra: The prisoners add that they denied the Day of Judgment; this completes in Saqar the same chain as surah 107: denial of the dīn, failed prayer, and neglect of the poor.
terra: The condemned person neither affirmed the truth nor prayed; the next ayah identifies denial and turning away as the paired stance.
terra: "وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ" repeats the denial-and-turning formula of 92:16 after failure to pray.

luna: Here the righteous give food to the miskīn, orphan, and captive, the opposite of withholding the meal and shared hearth in the source. | terra: The righteous feed food they love to a miskīn, orphan, and captive; the two vulnerable figures of surah 107 are welcomed to the meal.

luna: They explain that they feed others only for God’s sake; 76:8 gives the act, contrasting selfless sharing with the source’s household refusal. | terra: They feed solely for God's face and seek neither reward nor thanks, a precise reversal of the visible performance condemned in 107:6.

luna: The food-givers of 76:8-9 say they fear a severe day from their Lord; their forethought contrasts with the source’s refusal to share before punishment. | terra: The people who feed the poor, orphan, and captive explain that they fear a grim Day from their Lord; their sharing is joined to belief in the judgment denied in surah 107.

luna: God protects these givers from the evil of that day; 76:8-10 provide their food-sharing and motive, a positive boundary to the source’s fire. | terra: God protects those feeders from that Day's evil and grants brightness and joy, showing the counter-destination to the fire reached by those who refuse food.
luna: They are rewarded with a garden and silk after feeding others in 76:8-9, completing the opposite outcome to the source’s withheld hearth and fire.

luna: The condemned are told to go to what they denied; 77:30-32 describe their fire, echoing the source’s denial-to-fire sequence. | terra: Deniers are ordered to proceed toward what they denied; the command begins a fire scene that ends under the refrain of woe.

luna: The passage sends them toward a three-branched shadow; 77:31 says it gives neither coolness nor protection from flame, making this anti-shelter relevant to the source’s hearth. | terra: They are sent to a three-branched shadow, an apparent shelter that the next ayah denies any sheltering power.

luna: The supposed shade neither cools nor protects from flame; 77:30 introduces the shade, making a direct opposite to the source’s warming hearth. | terra: The shadow neither shades nor protects from flame; it is the direct opposite of the useful fire and shelter conjoined in the section's domestic hearth.

luna: The fire throws fortress-sized sparks; 77:31 has just denied any cooling shelter, extending the source’s shift from useful fire to punishment. | terra: The flame casts sparks as large as a building, expanding the small useful hearth into an overwhelming punitive fire immediately before the woe refrain.

luna: After the sparks, woe falls on the deniers, bringing together the source’s named وَيْل and fire-facing deniers. | terra: After the flame throws its sparks, the refrain says woe that Day to the deniers, joining وَيْل, denial, and fire in one unit.
terra: When the deniers are told to bow, they do not bow; this failed act of worship is the concrete cause immediately before the woe refrain in 77:49.
terra: "وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ" follows their refusal to bow, linking the woe of deniers to a failed bodily act of worship.

luna: The source’s fire root ص ل و appears in يَصْلَوْنَهَا, burning on the Day of Judgment. | terra: The wicked "يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ"; the named root means burning precisely on the Day of Judgment denied in 107:1.
luna: The condemned are not absent from that fire; 82:15 names the burning, extending its inescapable heat.
terra: "وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ" directs the same woe-cry at people whose economic practice takes fully and gives less.
terra: The defrauders demand full measure when receiving from others; their receptive hand is open only toward themselves.
terra: When measuring or weighing for others they cause loss, a commercial counterpart to withholding the small goods another person needs.

luna: The source names the cry وَيْل; here the same woe falls on deniers, the first step in a passage that then names their burning. | terra: "وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ" joins the section's disaster cry وَيْل to deniers before their burning is stated in 83:16.

luna: These are those who deny the Day of Judgment, echoing the larger surah’s opening denier; 83:16-17 complete this passage’s path to fire. | terra: The deniers are those who deny the Day of Judgment, exactly identifying the denial named at the opening of surah 107.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in لَصَالُوا الْجَحِيمِ, explicitly describing the condemned as burning in Hell. | terra: "ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُو الْجَحِيمِ" carries the named ص ل و root in its fire sense and fulfills the earlier وَيْل against the deniers.

luna: After the burning, they are told this is what they used to deny; 83:16 contributes the fire, making denial meet its consequence. | terra: The burning deniers are told that this is what they used to deny, making the punishment answer their earlier stance in its own words.
luna: This person receives his record from behind; 84:12 gives the fire that follows, resembling the source’s cited record-to-Hell sequence in Hāqqah.

luna: He cries out for destruction before the fire named in 84:12, continuing the record-to-punishment sequence. | terra: The recipient of the record behind his back will call for destruction, supplying a disaster cry immediately before ص ل و names his burning.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا, the burning fate of the person given the record from behind. | terra: "وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا" places the named root's fire sense directly after the condemned person's cry for ruin, the same sound-structure the section hears in وَيْل and الْمُصَلِّينَ.
luna: He had been joyful among his people; 84:14 says he thought he would not return, explaining the stance beside 84:12’s fire fate.
luna: He thought he would never return to God; 84:12 names the fire he faces, linking denial of return to the source’s judgment and fire image.
terra: "النَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ" presents a fire supplied with fuel, exactly one dictionary object of the section's صلاء, but here the fuelled hearth is an instrument of persecution.
terra: The trench-makers sit around the fuelled fire, "إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ"; it is the section's social hearth scene reversed into people calmly watching others burn.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ, burning in the greatest fire. | terra: The most wretched enters "النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ" through the ص ل و verb, another direct Qur'anic use of the root's punitive face.

luna: In that fire he neither dies nor lives; 87:12 names the burning, giving a stark form to the source’s bearing of heat and severity. | terra: In that fire he neither dies nor lives, sharpening the dictionary sense of having to endure an affair's heat and severity.

luna: The source’s fire root ص ل و appears in تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً, a person burning in fierce heat. | terra: Humiliated faces "تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً"; the same root states direct exposure to intensely hot fire.

luna: The fire-bound person is given water from a boiling spring; 88:4 supplies the burning and 88:6-7 the failed meal, reversing the household food scene. | terra: Faces burning in the intensely hot fire are made to drink from a boiling spring, extending the heat into a punitive household act of serving drink.

luna: Their only food is thorny plant; 88:4-5 place it in a burning, boiling setting, an opposite to the source’s nourishing shared meal. | terra: They have no food except a harsh thorny plant; after the fire and boiling drink, the meal itself becomes deprivation.

luna: This food neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger; 88:6 identifies it, contrasting the source’s meal withheld from the poor. | terra: That food neither nourishes nor removes hunger, reversing the sustaining food that the section says should reach the poor.
terra: The rebuke begins with failure to honor the orphan, placing the other vulnerable figure of surah 107 beside the refusal to urge poor-feeding in 89:18.

luna: The wording وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ repeats the failure to urge feeding the poor, with the source’s miskīn root س ك ن adding the hearth association. | terra: "وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ" is the plural counterpart of 107:3 and locates failure to urge poor-feeding amid greed and the coming of Hell.

luna: The same passage says they greedily consume inheritance after failing to urge food for the poor in 89:18, specifying the grasping conduct beside the source’s withholding. | terra: They consume inheritance voraciously; predatory eating stands beside their refusal to secure food for the poor.

luna: Their love of wealth is intense; following the refusal to urge food in 89:18-19, it explains the grasping that the source turns toward fire. | terra: Their immense love of wealth explains why the orphan and poor are excluded and prepares the judgment scene that follows.

luna: After the passage condemns failing to urge food for the poor and devouring inheritance greedily, Hell is brought forth; this makes the source’s withheld provision and final fire one sequence. | terra: Hell is brought forth on that Day after the rebuke for greed and neglected feeding, completing the same movement from an unshared table to fire.
luna: When Hell is brought forth in 89:23, the person regrets not having sent something ahead; it echoes the source’s record-to-fire sequence and its warning about withholding.

luna: The passage commends feeding in a day of hunger, reversing the source’s failure to urge food for the poor. | terra: The steep path includes feeding on a day of hunger; food shared at the moment of greatest need reverses the withheld hearth of the section.

luna: The next verse identifies an orphan near of kin as one who receives that food, specifying the vulnerable neighbor absent from the withheld hearth. | terra: The first named recipient is an orphan of near kin, answering the orphan who is pushed away in 107:2.

luna: The sequence names a miskīn in the dust as another recipient; the source’s miskīn root س ك ن is heard here against refusal to share food. | terra: The next recipient is "مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ", a poor person reduced to the dust; the named miskīn is restored to the shared meal.
luna: After feeding the orphan and needy in 90:14-16, the verse names faith, patience, and mercy; it completes the positive course opposed to the source’s withholding.
terra: Those who reject God's signs are identified as the people of the left immediately before the fire closes over them, supplying the denial side of 90:20's punishment.
terra: Those who reject God's signs have a fire closed over them; the passage makes refusal of the steep path of feeding terminate in an enclosing fire.

luna: The section itself names بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ as where this surah’s path begins; the tight-fisted self-sufficient person stands behind the withheld pot and ladle. | terra: The downward course begins with the person who is miserly and deems himself self-sufficient; this gives the moral starting point for the blazing fire later named in 92:14-15.
luna: After the tight-fisted person of 92:8 comes denial of the best; it develops the path toward the fire warned of in 92:14.
luna: This says the tight-fisted denier is eased toward hardship; the following fire passage makes that hard end concrete.
luna: His wealth will not avail when he falls; it sharpens the source’s claim that one who withholds provision ultimately faces fire.

luna: The warning names نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ, a blazing fire; 92:15-16 identify who burns there and why. | terra: God's warning "فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ" explicitly announces the blaze toward which the miser's course leads.

luna: The source’s ص ل و root appears in لَا يَصْلَاهَا, the act of entering and burning in that fire. | terra: "لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى" uses ص ل و for entering and enduring the blaze, the fire-bearing face heard beside الْمُصَلِّينَ in the section.

luna: The one who burns is described as having denied and turned away; 92:14-15 supply the warning and fire, linking refusal to the source’s outcome. | terra: The one who burns is identified as the person who denied and turned away, joining fire to the opening denial of surah 107.

luna: The God-fearing are kept away from the fire warned of in 92:14-16, a direct boundary to the source’s stingy person reaching punishment. | terra: The Godfearing person is kept far from the blaze; the principal boundary is that giving wealth in 92:18 leads away from the fire that receives the miser.

luna: This person gives his wealth to purify himself, the clear reversal of the tight-fisted person in 92:8 and the source’s withheld household provision. | terra: The Godfearing person gives his wealth to purify himself and is kept from the blaze; generosity is the direct counter-course to the miser of 92:8 and the withholders of the section.

luna: The giver has no favor to repay; 92:18 supplies his giving, contrasting with the source’s closed hand around ordinary provision. | terra: The giver is not spending to repay a favor owed to anyone, excluding social calculation from the generosity that keeps him from the blaze.

luna: His giving seeks only his Lord’s countenance; 92:18 states the act and 92:17 the escape from fire, completing the opposite motive and outcome. | terra: He gives only in seeking the face of his Most High Lord, supplying the inward sincerity opposite to worship performed to be seen.
luna: The giver will be satisfied after the wealth-giving in 92:18 and protection in 92:17, a positive end opposite the source’s fire-bound miser.
terra: The orphan must not be oppressed, a direct reversal of pushing the orphan away in surah 107.
terra: The petitioner must not be repelled, extending the open-handed household stance to the person who asks.
terra: Rivalry in accumulation distracts people, naming the possessive preoccupation that the surah later brings before Hell.
terra: Those distracted by accumulation are told they will surely see Hell, completing a concise movement from multiplying possessions to the fire.

luna: The source’s word وَيْل recurs over the wealth-hoarder of this passage; 104:2 and 104:4-6 connect the hoarding to kindled fire. | terra: "وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ" begins another sequence in which the woe-cry falls upon a selfish accumulator and ends in a kindled fire.

luna: This person amasses and counts wealth, giving a concrete form of the source’s withholding before the fire scene in 104:4-9. | terra: The target gathers wealth and repeatedly counts it; the hoarded good supplies the social shape behind the fire announced later in the surah.

luna: He thinks wealth will make him last forever; 104:2 names the accumulation and 104:4-9 overturn that confidence with fire. | terra: The accumulator imagines his wealth has made him immortal; this names the self-sufficiency behind his hoarding before the surah overturns it with the kindled fire.

luna: He is flung into al-Ḥuṭamah; 104:5-6 identify it as God’s kindled fire, turning the source’s woe into a fire scene. | terra: The hoarder will be thrown into the Crusher, turning private accumulation into forcible exposure to punishment.
luna: The question asks what al-Ḥuṭamah is; 104:6 answers with kindled fire, defining the punishment that follows the source’s withholding image.

luna: The answer is نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ, kindled fire; 104:4 names the person flung into it, echoing the source’s useful hearth turned punishment. | terra: The Crusher is identified as "نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ", a deliberately kindled fire that converts the section's useful hearth into judgment.

luna: The fire rises over hearts; 104:6 names its kindling, extending the endured-heat image of the source. | terra: God's kindled fire rises over the hearts, showing that the hoarder's apparently external conduct has an inward seat reached by the flame.

luna: The fire is closed over them; 104:6-7 supply the fire and its reach, continuing the punishment scene. | terra: The fire is closed over the hoarders; their closed store returns as an inescapably closed fire, repeating the enclosing-fire end of 90:20.
luna: They are confined among extended pillars; 104:8 supplies the closure around the fire, completing this sustained punishment scene.

terra: God feeds Quraysh against hunger and secures them against fear; divine provision and household safety form the direct moral background against which refusing the poor person's food becomes ingratitude.
luna: His wealth will not avail him; 111:3-4 bring the fire and its fuel, paralleling the source’s refusal to share provision before facing fire.

luna: The source’s root ص ل و appears in سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ, a direct statement that he will burn in a flaming fire. | terra: "سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ" uses the named root for burning in a flame, while the following ayah supplies the firewood image.

luna: The source dictionary form الصلاء includes fuel; this verse calls her حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ, a carrier of firewood in the same punishment scene. | terra: The fire-bound man's wife is "حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ", a carrier of firewood; the section's fuel sense becomes part of the punitive household pair.
